<explanation>
Based on the file tree and README information, this project is clearly a Kubernetes operator for managing ClickHouse clusters on Kubernetes. Its purpose is to deploy, manage, and upgrade ClickHouse clusters—as well as related components like ClickHouse Keeper and metrics exporting—with a strong focus on automation using Kubernetes custom resources and reconciliation patterns. The operator code, written in Go, is organized into multiple directories such as cmd/operator and pkg/controller for the core business logic, pkg/apis for custom resource definitions, pkg/model for cluster models and configuration generators, and additional directories for deployments (Helm charts, manifests, etc.) and tests.

To create an accurate system design diagram that reflects this project’s architecture, follow these guidelines:

1. Identify the main components:
   • Kubernetes API Server – external component with which the operator interacts.
   • ClickHouse Operator – the core application that contains:
       ○ Controllers/Reconciliation loops (visible in pkg/controller/chi for ClickHouse installations and pkg/controller/chk for ClickHouse Keeper).
       ○ Custom Resource Definitions (in pkg/apis/...) implementing resources like ClickHouseInstallation, ClickHouseOperatorConfiguration, etc.
       ○ Client libraries, informers, and listers (located in pkg/client) that monitor Kubernetes events and facilitate reconciliation.
       ○ Sub-components for configuration, templating, and resource management defined in pkg/model, pkg/chop, pkg/util.
   • Metrics Exporter – a secondary component (see cmd/metrics_exporter) that likely gathers and exposes metrics, integrating with external monitoring tools.
   • User-managed ClickHouse Clusters – the clusters created, configured, and upgraded by the operator.
   • External Tools and Integrations:
       ○ Prometheus – for gathering metrics (exported via the metrics exporter).
       ○ Grafana – dashboards and visualization as provided by deployment configurations.
       ○ External storages and services (persistent volumes, OpenEBS, Minio, etc.) as configured via custom templates and installation manifests.
       
2. Show relationships and interactions:
   • Draw directional arrows from the Kubernetes API Server towards the Operator to indicate event watch and CR change notifications. Also, depict the operator using Kubernetes client libraries to update or create resources.
   • Show the Operator issuing commands that result in changes to fundamental Kubernetes objects (Pods, Services, Deployments, ConfigMaps, Secrets, StatefulSets, etc.) that run one or more ClickHouse clusters.
   • Illustrate how the Metrics Exporter gathers metrics from these managed clusters and then exports them (using REST endpoints or Prometheus exporters) to Prometheus.
   • Depict external integrations such as Helm deployments, operator Hub installations, and links to Prometheus and Grafana dashboards.

3. Highlight the architectural patterns and design principles:
   • Emphasize the Operator Pattern with a controller-based design where custom controllers (in separate packages for “chi” and “chk”) reconcile the desired state defined in custom resources.
   • Note the modular structure, with clear separations between API definitions, business/application logic, and client library implementations.
   • Include CI/CD pipelines (visible in/.github/workflows) and deployment procedures (Helm charts in deploy/helm, and scripts under deploy/) as remembered external support elements.
   • Mention key design principles such as extensibility (with templating and configurations in the “config” and “deploy/builder” folders) and observability (enabled by metrics exporting and integrated monitoring).

4. Include relevant technologies, frameworks, or libraries:
   • Go language (with modules listed in go.mod and go.sum).
   • Kubernetes client-go libraries (used in pkg/client/*).
   • CRD, Informer, and Lister patterns.
   • Helm and YAML deployment manifests.
   • CI/CD workflows defined in the GitHub actions directory.
   • Monitoring integrations with Prometheus and Grafana.

5. Tailoring the diagram to this operator project:
   • For this full-stack Kubernetes operator, clearly separate the cluster’s control plane from the operator’s internal components. The diagram should show how the operator’s various sub-components (controllers, metrics exporter, custom resources) interact with the Kubernetes API and with the ClickHouse clusters they manage.
   • Make sure to reflect how configuration and templating are handled—include a “Configuration Manager / Templating Engine” box representing files under deploy/builder/templates-config and the extensive “config” directories.
   • Indicate test and deployment pipelines as supplementary systems (for instance, CI pipelines and the automated builds in the “dev” and “.github/workflows” directories).

6. Additional diagram elements and formatting guidelines:
   • Use clear labels for each component, e.g., “Kubernetes API Server”, “ClickHouse Operator Core”, “Custom Controller: CHI”, “Custom Controller: CHK”, “Metrics Exporter”, “Prometheus”, “ClickHouse Cluster – Instances”, “Persistent Storage Handler”, etc.
   • Use directional arrows to indicate flow of events (for instance, from Kubernetes API Server to Operator controllers, then from Operator to Kubernetes resources or metrics output to Prometheus).
   • Consider a color-coding scheme (for example, blue for external services like API Server, green for operator core components, orange for monitoring components, etc.) or different shapes (rectangles for processes, cylinders for databases/storage, parallelograms for external integrations) to visually distinguish between types of components.
   • Be very detailed – include all major elements like the command-line entry points under cmd/operator and cmd/metrics_exporter, the client libraries, and configuration/deployment tools that ensure the operator functions in a Kubernetes environment.

By following these steps and ensuring each crucial component and interaction is clearly represented, you will produce a comprehensive system design diagram that accurately reflects the Altinity Kubernetes Operator for ClickHouse. This diagram will be instrumental in both communicating architecture to new developers and supporting further development or troubleshooting by the team.
</explanation>
